So I installed the game before jumping into SM2 to get a grasp of the story, so how does it hold up in 2026? Honestly, not bad.

The graphics are definitely outdated, especially the scenery, its all low res gray. I only had two crashes and one soft lock, so not too bad overall. The gameplay still holds up nicely, and the hack-and-slash combat feels fluid. The weapons feel unique and useful, each shining in its own area, and experimenting with different combinations was surprisingly rewarding. Enemy variety is very limited, but I never felt like any section overstayed its welcome, although some areas came very close to that.

The plot was surprisingly good since I expected it to be just filler content. The environmental storytelling was on point, even if 90% of what you see is shades of gray (and green, I guess).

So if you're looking to get some backstory for SM2, this is a great 7-hour adventure. If you're looking purely for the gameplay, though, there are better options out there.

I wasn´t much into Warhammer 40K´s world so I think I couldn´t appreciate some details enough and still I firmly believe this game is an undeniable jewel. I would recommend it 1000000%, I loved every bit of it, the combat is complex enough that it feels like fun, at least to me, and everything else is very well built. I would recommend playing it before playing the second entry in the franchise (the one that came out in 2024 I believe) although is not completely necessary, only for the references to this one. I´m gonna dive right into the rest of Warhammer after this!

I remember getting this game on its original release date. I barely gave it a chance, maybe just the first mission. I'm so happy I came back to give it another try. I'm not really up on the 40k lore but I enjoyed the story of this game. Graphics are decent for the age. Ran flawlessly. Gameplay is good enough. Controls can be awkward at times. Overall it's a lot of fun though.
